title: Network Topology
markdown:
**Network topology** describes the arrangement of nodes and connections in a network.

- A **logical topology** is a conceptual representation of how devices operate at particular layers of abstraction.
- A **physical topology** details how devices are physically connected.

Both logical and physical topologies can be represented as visual diagrams.

### Topology Comparison

| Parameter | Bus | Ring | Star | Mesh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Best For | Small networks | Small–Medium | Small–Large | Small (critical) |
| Cable Required | Least (1 backbone) | Moderate (*n* links) | Moderate (*n* links) | Most (*n(n−1)/2* links) |
| Traffic Handling | Low (collisions) | Medium (token-based) | High (switched) | High (dedicated links) |
| Fault Tolerance | Low (backbone break fails all) | Low (ring break fails all) | Moderate (hub is single point of failure) | Very High (redundant paths) |
| Cost | Low | Moderate | Moderate | Very High |

> A **hybrid topology** combines two or more basic topologies — for example, a star backbone connecting three bus subnetworks.

More: [Network Topologies — Advantages & Disadvantages](https://www.comparitech.com/net-admin/network-topologies-advantages-disadvantages/)
